builder_plan.scenario: You already need task-specific training and want to reduce its memory or compute cost.
builder_plan.change: Change only the training technique on a small controlled run after checking prerequisites.
builder_plan.baseline: Your current training recipe with the same model, data split, and evaluation.
steps: Locate the paper's implementation and check its license, model support, data needs, and hardware requirements. Stop here if you cannot obtain the required artifacts.
Save a small set of representative product tasks and expected outcomes. Keep evaluation tasks out of any training or tuning, and choose quality and cost limits before running.
Run the baseline and the proposed change on identical inputs. Keep other settings fixed and repeat paired runs to expose variation.
Save per-task outputs, failures, timings, and all usage costs. Review regressions before expanding the test.
builder_plan.measure: Held-out quality, peak memory, training time, and full compute cost to the target quality.
builder_plan.decision: Keep the change only if it meets your preselected quality and latency limits and improves the metric you care about after setup and operating costs. Otherwise retain the baseline. This is an exploration plan, not a validated recommendation.

title: From What Is Used to What Is Missing: Rethinking Dynamic Rank in LoRA
summary: GEAR replaces static or heuristic dynamic-rank allocation in LoRA with a tangent-normal decomposition that estimates the normal-space spectrum to guide locally optimal rank expansion and task-induced initialization. The cost is added implementation complexity and matrix-free spectral estimation overhead during training, while reduced trainable parameters lower optimizer memory on a 24 GB GPU. It can fail if the local quadratic assumption poorly approximates the loss landscape, if matrix-free normal-spectrum estimates are noisy, or if gains observed on evaluated language and vision benchmarks do not transfer to the reader's tasks and models.
rationale: It is directly relevant to single-GPU LoRA fine-tuning and reports improved average performance with substantially fewer trainable parameters, but its rank-expansion gains and spectral-estimation overhead require validation on the reader's workloads.
technique: GEAR: Geometric Rank Evolution for LoRA

claims.statement: GEAR replaces static or heuristic dynamic-rank allocation in LoRA with a tangent-normal decomposition that estimates the normal-space spectrum to guide locally optimal rank expansion and task-induced initialization. The cost is added implementation complexity and matrix-free spectral estimation overhead during training, while reduced trainable parameters lower optimizer memory on a 24 GB GPU. It can fail if the local quadratic assumption poorly approximates the loss landscape, if matrix-free normal-spectrum estimates are noisy, or if gains observed on evaluated language and vision benchmarks do not transfer to the reader's tasks and models.

On LLaMA3-8B, raises the average commonsense score from 86.61 to 88.45 while reducing trainable parameters from 42.0M to 14.4M; the improvement is in accuracy points and parameter count, not a multiplicative factor.
